_doc: Per-function emit progress -- how far each function has got, and nothing else. Version controlled, because a run that is interrupted has to be able to resume from disk with no conversation context. `status` advances pending -> emitted -> reviewed -> committed; `failed` and `skip` are terminal and both must appear in the closing report. `in_flight` is written by the emitter before it touches anything and is deliberately left UNCOMMITTED: the landing commit carries it on to `committed`, so an entry still saying `in_flight` at the start of a run is the one trace a killed session leaves saying which function was in the air. The next run's recovery stage discards that function's working-tree residue under src/ and tests/ and rewrites the entry as `interrupted`. Neither `in_flight` nor `interrupted` is terminal, so next_batch.py hands the address out again exactly as it would a `pending` one -- nothing about the function was judged, it just never finished. `body_size` is the Ghidra body size the emit was made against: on resume it is compared with ghidra_snapshot/functions.txt, and an entry whose function has since changed size is retired and re-emitted rather than being skipped as done. There is deliberately no commit hash here -- one cannot be recorded inside the commit that creates it; the landing commit carries the address in its subject, so `git log --oneline --grep \"@ <addr>\"` finds it. Which file a function belongs in is NOT decided here: routing.json owns that, and next_batch.py reports rather than believes a `target` here that disagrees with it. Only functions that have been started appear; the roster comes from routing.json.
